shola inkose.name: Shola Inkose
shola inkose.species: Depowered Mutant, temporary repowered by Terrigenesis
shola inkose.origin: ===Student in the University of Chicago=== Born in Genosha, Shola was smuggled out as a child as a foreign exchange student. After he grew older, he attended the University of Chicago. When Cassandra Nova had Wild Sentinels destroy Genosha, Shola lost his entire family who had been living on the island at the time. He was left utterly alone, not only because of the loss of his family and home, but also with the revocation of his student visa when the United Nations declared Genosha a terrorist state due to the activities of "Magneto". To add insult to injury, Shola had been in contact with a telepath on Genosha the moment that the island was destroyed, leaving him with a mental imprint of the "death-moment" of everyone who died on Genosha during the horrific attack. Every time he closed his eyes and entered a REM state, he experienced another death first-hand from that terrible day. As a result he couldn't sleep and hadn't slept since. After the attack, Shola briefly remained at the University of Chicago where he met Kitty Pryde and Xuân Cao Mạnh after helping them with an incident in the physics department caused by the anti-mutant hate group Purity. After this episode, his flat was targeted by Purity members. Befriending the two former X-Men and Tom More, a Purity member he saved from the previous incident who had come to fight alongside his teammates, he started hanging out with the three, helping Kitty to restore her flat trashed by the F.B.I. and anti-mutant neighborhood, and subtly threatening Tom. He later helped Kitty and Shan defeat a few Wild Sentinels that attacked them. Shola was instrumental in their destruction as Karma's telepathic powers were useless on the machines, and they quickly adapted to Shadowcat's offensive phasing ability. During the debate opposing Alice Tremaine and Purity to tolerate the mutant presence in the university, Shola tried to get violent but was calmed down by Kitty, as a use of powers and a fight would only give satisfaction to the racists. Just at the moment he left the room with Karma for a walk, the Wild Sentinels invaded the campus. Helped morally by Karma, Shola managed to destroy all of the Sentinels, saving the students. With the battle won, Kitty, Tom, Xian, and Shola were free to relax together in Chicago. ===Genoshan Excalibur=== He was next seen captured and placed in stasis by a group of Genoshan Magistrates who used to dominate the island before Magneto took over. Along with the Prime Sentinel Karima Shapandar, it appeared that they were going to be the secret weapons of the Magistrates to take back the island. However, the airplane that was carrying them crashed and Shola found himself on the side of the ragtag members of the newest incarnation of Excalibur. His abilities were indispensable to Professor X in the demolition and reconstruction of his homeland. ===M-Day=== During the Decimation, Shola was one of the many mutants who lost their mutant abilities. When Quicksilver came to Genosha, offering to restore their powers using the Terrigen Mists, he wasn't interested first, as he feared to have his nightmares back with his mutant gifts. He eventually took the cure, and was indeed forced to stay awake, as his visions were back. He was later taken into medical care with the other refugees by the O*N*E, at the same hospital where Callisto had been sent when his powers overwhelmed her. The effects of the Mists eventually wore off, leaving him powerless once more.

He was part of the Blue Team. ===Reservation X=== Shola refused to give up his mutation and together with twenty specimens transported for new housing, where some of the mutants were not happy with this turn. When Nomi decided to change the leader of mutants and arranged a vote, Shola was chosen. After voting, the company traveled to the village, which was called Utopia, where they were going to make the Earth more hospitable, then was sent to material assistance from the helicopter stark, of which was brought food. In the morning Shola with other mutants learned that Blackheart pulled mutated seeds. When the evening began with a press conference arranged Tony Stark, Shola attended together with the rest of the mutants, and the assembled people in Utopia, and listened to the speech Kitty Pryde. thumb|Mach Two's group, with Shola, leaves Utopia Soon Shola with other mutants sees that to the Utopia got dehydrated Husk. On the following morning he is present during the meeting mutants, arranged Kitty Pryde. When the blast from the place where grown seeds, then Shola and some mutants went with Nomi in search of a new place of accommodation. ===Natural Resources=== Two weeks later, Utopia flourished, and Shola group Mach Two hid from surveillance Jimmy Hudson. The next day Shola together with James met Jimmy, who appointed a meeting for them. Hearing that the Hudson offers to work together and that it does not support the peaceful intention Kitty Pryde, Shola as James agrees to cooperate with him, but he asks them to take Nomi weapons Kitty. Later Shola with Warpath tell Psylocke and Mach Two, that they are faced with the Hudson, and agreed to work with him together. shooter female.name: Shooter (Female)
shooter female.origin: Shooter was a member of Geronimo Crowe's resistance group who was task to fight against the Administrator and his Watchtower. She helped rescue Wolverine after he had been captured by Deadpool and the Administrator's team the Scourge. Shooter engaged the Administrator's personal guard in battle by using an energy weapon built within her cybernetic arm. Once they took care of the "goon squad", she wanted to finish off Deadpool even though his reason for helping the Administrator was to heal the mutant Siryn who laid in suspended animation inside a stasis tube. Shooter got trigger happy and fired a blast that hit Deadpool in the head while knocking the tube to the ground. This caused Siryn to wake up while she used her voice to crack the glass open thus releasing her from the pod. Shooter became bewildered by Theresa's sonic voice asking if this was normal. Wolverine conveyed that that the return of her mutant abilities was a minor miracle. After a brief discussion between Theresa and Logan, Shooter went along with her team to another Watchtower safehouse but after taking out one of the guards they found out the Administrator was only here as a projected hologram leading them to another dead end.

short circuit.name: Short Circuit
short circuit.origin: Short Circuit was a grandchild of Lilith, and thus part-demon himself. On learning of his ancestry, he became determined to earn her favor, and murdered at least fourteen boys as offerings to her. He was eventually captured, imprisoned, and sentenced to death. As he was placed in the electric chair, his demonic powers finally became active, absorbing the electricity and giving him the ability to create portals into other worlds. Now immensely powerful, he took over the prison, killing most of the staff and guards and freeing his fellow prisoners. Using his powers, he transported many people into other worlds, driving many of them insane. When the Nightstalkers came to investigate reports of strange occurrences at the prison, he attacked them, throwing Hannibal King into an alternate dimension. When Frank Drake tried to use an electrical gun against him, he absorbed the energy, becoming even more powerful. Eventually, the remaining Nightstalkers were able to find and rescue Hannibal King, and realizing that Short Circuit needed to absorb electricity to power his abilities, they shut down the prison's power systems. Without an external source of electricity, Short Circuit's powers consumed his own energy, reducing him to a pile of ash.

shortpack.name: Shortpack
shortpack.origin: The mutant known as Shortpack is the nephew of now-deceased FBI agent and mutant-sympathizer Fred Duncan. If not for the meditative exercises he learned from Professor Charles Xavier, he likely would have shrunk to a microscopic size. Unfortunately for him, he cannot control his power to grow or shrink any further, and so he remains about 8 inches tall. Shortpack was recruited by Professor Xavier to be a field handler for the clandestine operatives in his employ. Shortpack's first agent was Prudence (Agent 16), who was seemingly killed by the arms dealer Steinbeck. The next agent to be assigned to him was the former mutant terrorist/freedom fighter, Mystique, but when the two met in Cuba for the first time, Shortpack did not know about her terrorist background. After handling Mystique on a few missions, Shortpack was contacted by the Quiet Man, who offered him a way to exact vengeance on Steinbeck for killing Prudence. He tried to get Fantomex to kill Steinbeck for him, but was refused, though Fantomex brought him to what he thought was Steinbeck's lair. Instead, Shortpack found that his target was his benefactor - the Quiet Man - was Prudence's mind in Steinbeck's body, and the exchange had driven her mad. S/he captured Shortpack and used him as bait for Mystique, who had replaced her. Shortpack was eventually rescued by Mystique, and presumably still works for Xavier.

shorty harris.name: Shorty Harris
shorty harris.origin: Assigned by his editor to investigate those who supplied weapons to indigenous people in the Congo, Shorty Harris traveled to Africa. During the investigation he discovered that a group of hunters intended to capture a large anthropomorphic ape with four arms. Being an animal lover, Shorty ran to the Beast's aid and saved him from capture. Soon after he was captured by the natives and held prisoner in their village to hand him over to the hunter who sold him weapons, the same hunter who wanted to capture the Beast. Recognizing Shorty as the one who had prevented the capture of the Beast, he ordered the natives to eliminate him, but the Beast came to Shorty's aid, who revealed himself to be a powerful alien looking for a human worthy of hearing his message. As a gesture of goodwill to other species all zoos on Earth were shut down.

shou lao.name: Shou-Lao
shou lao.origin: ===Early Life=== Shou-Lao (Chinese: 壽老, Shòu Lǎo) was an immortal dragon from a dark plane of existence who became the source of power for K'un-Lun. ===1,000,000 BC=== thumb|right|Shou-Lao in 1,000,000 BC Fan Fei was brought for execution by Shou-Lao for breaking a forbidden rule of K'un-Lun: teaching their sacred traditions to cavemen. These cavemen were also brought to be executed. All of them died except Fan Fei, who killed the sacred dragon with her bare hands and claimed her title as the first Iron Fist. ===Quan Yaozu=== Many years after Fan Fei killed Shou-Lao, the dragon had reincarnated and already found his way back to his home dimension. Changming, an ancient trickster, used dark arts to open a portal to Shou-Lao's dimension, allowing Shou-Lao and other dark creatures to enter K'un-Lun. Changming used the dragon to conquer K'un-Lun and terrorize the citizens. While Shou-Lao was sleeping in a cave, Quan Yaozu confronted and defeated him, gaining the power of the Iron Fist. Quan would use Shou-Lao's scales as one of the many materials to create the Book of the Iron Fist. ===Hyborian Age=== During the Age of Conan, circa 10,000 BC, Shou-Lao was invoked by men of Khitai. ===Molten Heart=== According to Cybelle, during a performance of the dragon riders of K'un-Lun for the entertainment of its Yu-Ti, Shou-Lao went berserk and attacked the city's leader. He was slain by Quan-St'ar, who cut out the dragon's heart. Enraged at this, Yu-Ti banished Quan-St'ar from the city and revived the dragon by melting its heart. He then placed the molten heart further inside the dragon's sacred cavern. From this moment forward, in order to receive the power of the Iron Fist, each potential combatant had to defeat Shou-Lao, and then kill him by plunging their fists into its molten heart. Shou-Lao was reborn over 66 times. ===1878 AD=== A Ch'i-Lin entered K'un-Lun through Kwai Jun-Fan's heart in an attempt to consume the egg of Shou-Lao. Lei Kung the Thunderer and the warriors of K'un-Lun held back the beast, successfully protecting the vulnerable egg. ===Danny Rand=== thumb|left|Facing Danny Rand In modern days, Danny Rand defeated the dragon, and in the course of the battle, had the dragon-shaped scar burned on his chest. After defeating Shou-Lao, he plunged his hands into the brazier containing the dragon's molten heart seven times, and it charged him with the power of the Iron Fist. ===Immortal Iron Fist=== Lei Kung the Thunderer assigned Davos to guard the egg that would one day hatch into the reborn Shou-Lao. A Ch'i-Lin attempted to reach the egg and consume it, but was stopped by the Iron Fist. The egg of Shou-Lao hatched shortly after. ===Avengers vs. X-Men=== When Cyclops and the X-Men were fighting the Avengers in K'un-Lun, Hope Summers and the Thunderer came riding upon Shou-Lao. The dragon blasted Cyclops, who was empowered by the Phoenix Force, with its fire. Unfortunately, the dragon was too young and weak to put up a fight, and its riders were forcibly dismounted by Cyclops' return attack. However, Hope was able to unleash a combination of dragon energy, fire, and chaos magic to banish Cyclops to the Moon. ===Iron Fist: The Living Weapon=== ====Attacked by The One and Davos==== thumb|left|Decapitated by The One and his undead ninjas Shou-Lao was on the verge of death for reasons unknown when the people of K'un-Lun held a ceremony, hosted by the new Yu-Ti, Lei Kung, to prepare for the dragon’s passing. The people of K'un-Lun planned to consume the flesh of Shou-Lao, but were interrupted by the arrival of The One and his army of undead ninjas. The One and his army rampaged through the city and decapitated Shou-Lao, killing him. Around the same time, Davos and a group of undead ninjas entered the chamber housing the egg of the next incarnation of Shou-Lao. Davos attempted to kill the Thunderer and destroy the egg, but a young monk named Pei secured the egg and fled to New York. ====Birth of Gork==== thumb|right|Gork licking Pei's face While fleeing from Davos and his group of undead ninjas, Pei dropped down through a manhole, causing the egg of Shou-Lao to fall out of her backpack. The egg quickly hatched, giving birth to the next incarnation of Shou-Lao the Undying. Pei nicknamed the young dragon "Gork" due to the sound it made. ====Killed by Davos==== After the arrival of Zhu Rong to New York City, Davos urged the people of K'un-Lun to flee back to their city through the Randall Machine inside Rand Tower. Disapproving the decision of Danny Rand's allies to stay and help Danny, Davos snapped Gork's neck. This disrupted Danny's chi and left the people inside Rand Tower defenseless against Zhu Rong's attacks. As Gork's spirit left his body, the dragon saw Pei's courage and desire to protect others, and chose her to be the next Iron Fist. Gork's chi then transferred to Pei, granting her a dragon-shaped scar on her back and the power of the Iron Fist. ====Resurrected by Pei==== Pei, using a technique from a spec

fields.notes: Shou-Lao's history as a performing dragon as recounted in Master of Kung Fu Annual #1 has most likely been effectively retconned. In later comics, this part of Shou-Lou's lore is ignored and overwritten. Shou-Lao's dragon-shaped scar on his chest was left as a result of the removal of his heart. Afterwards, when a person fought Shou-Lao and pressed against this scar, they were burned by it. The resulting mark on their own body appeared as a mirror image, facing left. The dragon's scar typically had the head facing right, but it was sometimes mistakenly depicted in reverse. Shou-Lao appeared to possess the ability to alter his appearance upon being reborn. He was most often depicted as a serpent-like dragon without wings or limbs. However, some incarnations were shown to have wings and/or limbs, whereas others combined a serpent-like body with short, stout claws. When Shou-Lao died or was about to die of natural causes (such as times when there was no need for a new Iron Fist, and thus no need to kill the dragon), the citizens of K'un-Lun would consume the beast and feed on its chi. Shou-Lao's chi was also infused into the rivers of K'un-Lun, giving nourishment to the Tree of Immortality and its fruit, which granted immortality to those who consumed it. Danny Rand claimed there were 66 incarnations of Shou-Lao (not including Gork), based on the 66 Iron Fists before him. Despite this claim, there must be more than 66 incarnations of Shou-Lao due to the existence of incarnations who lived and died before the birth of a new Iron Fist. Additionally, a Ch'i-Lin said that 66 Iron Fists died before Danny, making him the 67th Iron Fist. This would suggest at least 67 incarnations of Shou-Lao before Gork. However, this statement comes with a caveat: the Ch'i-Lin was likely exaggerating, given that not every Iron Fist before Danny had died at this point, such as Quan Yaozu and Resourceful Snake.

shower.name: Shower
shower.species: Artificial being created by Mojo by using Neoplasm to resemble the Storm from X-Men.
shower.origin: Shower was one of the X-Babies created by Mojo from neoplasm to replace the original X-Men, whose death had caused a drop in ratings. Mojo was going to destroy them, but the X-Babies escaped alongside Mojo's pilot, Ricochet Rita. The group fled in Mojo's Crossover House and in the ensuing battle with Mojo's forces, escaped into Earth-616, with Rita being captured in the process and secretly converted into "The Agent" and sent after them. The group discovered Kitty Pryde on a train and upon startling her awake, Kitty phased out of the train. The group then had to return Excalibur but had no forms of communication and were being pursued by the Agent, who captured several of the X-Babies by tricking them into signing contracts. The captured were freed when Kitty removed the signatures from the contracts. They captured the Agent during a fight between him and the X-Babies and Excalibur and Phoenix restored Rita. The X-Babies agreed to return to Mojo if he gave Rita her freedom. Shower and the X-Babies returned to Mojoworld alongside Rita as their guardian and had a list of demands that Mojo had to meet for them to return to work. After Mojo was usurped by Longshot and Dazzler, Gog and MaGog set out to kill the X-Babies. Shower and several others fled to Earth-616 and sought help from Phoenix and Iceman who protected the X-Babies until Dazzler arrived and ordered the pair to stand down. She allowed the X-Babies to come and lives in the royal palace for their protection. Shower was one of the X-Babies who helped Wolverine defeat the Warwolves disguised as his teammates and enemies that Mojo II was using to help return the Mojoverse to its television watching state. Some time after this, the X-Babies constructed the Clubhouse for Gifted Youngsters in the Umbrella Forest and were lead by Charlie X who was considered their "Big Brother". Here, the X-Babies tried to save the Pix from the Brotherhood of Mutant Bullies. Failing in their mission the X-Babies returned to their base, only to be attacked and captured by Centennials (Parade balloons turned into Sentinels). The X-Babies were forced to take part in a game show designed by Funhouse (an Evil Baby version of Arcade), which included both quiz and deathtraps. The group failed at the quiz sections but were able to beat the traps and were eventually freed by Cyke and Locksteed. Funhouse threatened to turn the Brotherhood back into neoplasm if the X-Babies did not return and they were about to agree to this when Charlie X showed up with reinforcements and saved the X-Babies.

shredder.name: Shredder
shredder.origin: Shredder was a killer for hire who enjoyed torturing others. He fought Wolverine years ago and nearly killed him. When drug dealers Sid and Whitie two-timed him, Harry Gavino hired the Shredder to go after them. Sid and Whitie, having survived after the plane they were flying on crashed in the Canadian wilderness. Shredder later learned that Sid Whitie from an elderly couple that the criminals had stolen a motorhome from them. Shredded thanked the couple by killing them. Whitie, while driving the motorhome, crashed it after one of his hostages attacked him. Whitie's back was broken and left behind by Sid. Shredder found Whitie and killed him after getting the info he needed. Shredder eventually found Sid at Lake Vague and killed him. One of Sid's hostages told him of a safe that she could open if she let the other hostage, her son, live. Shredded agreed and took a boat out onto Lake Vague. During Shredder's mission, he was being tracked by Wolverine and the Hulk. When Shredder tossed one of the hostages into the water, Wolverine asked Hulk to save the hostage while he went after Shredder. Wolverine boarded Shredder's boat and battled him, eventually crashing the boat on dry land. Shredder badly hurt Wolverine while he was stunned, but Wolverine sliced his right arm off and left him to be eaten by a mountain lion. Shredder later appeared as one of the many souls in Hell that Marduk Kurios sent to fight Wolverine.

shrub.name: Shrub
shrub.origin: Shrub works with his partner Pockets Possum as couriers. One day Groot hired Pockets Postal to deliver him to Lord Rakzoon. Upon making the delivery, Pockets and Shrub were accused of being thieves and thrown in Lord Rakzoon's torture dungeon. After making a deal with the imprisoned former dictator of the planet, High Ruler Nosaj, both Pockets and Shrub tried to have Rocket and Groot killed; however, their plan backfired after their squabbling caused Nosaj to decided to have all four killed instead. The quartet escaped the palace, but Pockets still held resentment towards Rocket for imprisoning them, and almost getting them killed. Rocket responded by stealing Pockets' ship, leaving Pockets and Shrub stranded, for which the possum vowed revenge against Rocket.

shu han.name: Shu Han
shu han.origin: Shu Han was selected by the Claw to be his future wife when she was still a child. Growing up, Han became a Nobel Prize-winning physicist and Olympic athlete in track and field. When the Claw's agents abducted Han to force her into the arranged marriage, she was able to contact the Avengers, who came to rescue her. The Claw, upon learning about Han's unwillingness to marry him, released her.

shu hu.name: Shu-Hu
shu hu.origin: Shu-Hu was the runner-up in the tournament that Quan Yaozu won, earning the right to confront Shou-Lao the Undying, whom he defeated to become the Iron Fist. Shu-Hu was then charged with becoming The One, the final opponent whom all who become the Iron Fist must defeat. The "Challenge of The One" determined if an Iron Fist was truly worthy of their station, and if they would be given the opportunity to consume the fruit of immortality from the Tree of Immortality. Shu-Hu went on to kill many Iron Fists who failed to defeat him over the years. He longed to become the Iron Fist himself, but was denied, regardless of his skill. When Phineas Randall's transglobal airship crashed into K'un-Lun, Yu-Ti became enamored with the outworlder and asked Shu-Hu to allow Phineas' son, Orson, to defeat him and cement his position as the next Iron Fist. Disgusted at this, Shu-Hu refused and left K'un-Lun, but was secretly replaced with a mechanical impostor that would comply with the Yu-Ti's wishes. Shu-Hu was joined by others who were opposed to K'un-Lun's growing corruption, and together they opened seven houses of martial arts on the isle of Liu-Shi. There they trained for a century, plotting to one day defeat the Iron Fist and reclaim their home. Under the alias of the Divine Wolf of the House of the Wolf, and as a member of the Council of Liu-Shi, Shu-Hu then had Choshin of the House of the Bull lure Danny Rand to Liu-Shi for a tournament, where he planned to defeat the outworlder and claim the chi absorbed from Shou-Lao to facilitate his return to K'un-Lun as a conqueror; however, Danny Rand eventually defeated him in combat.

shu hu android.name: Shu-Hu (Android)
shu hu android.origin: When Shu-Hu, The One, refused to deliberately lose his match in the Challenge of The One, which was intended to prove Orson Randall, son of Phineas Randall, worthy of the title of Iron Fist, Yu-Ti replaced him with a mechanical being that would obey without question. This android went on to face Danny Rand after he defeated Shou-Lao and gained the power of the Iron Fist. However, The One was programmed by Yu-Ti to lose this fight. As such, Danny defeated The One, revealing it to be an android in the process. This victory "proved" that Danny was worthy of the title of Iron Fist, and also won him the right to consume the fruit of immortality from the Tree of Immortality, which he refused. The One's body was taken out of K'un-Lun, since technology was not allowed in the city, and thrown into a deep crevasse. There, it bonded to the dormant body of Wendell Rand and took his head. It then absorbed his memories and believed itself to be Wendell, becoming obsessed with resurrecting Heather Rand, Wendell's wife. First, he got revenge on K'un Lun for abandoning him. He burned down the city and killed many people, including the Yu-Ti, and an incarnation of Shou-Lao. When Iron Fist discovered this, he went after The One and discovered that the android wore his father's face and had also stolen the faces of the Thunderer and Harold Meachum. The One used Danny's rage to distract him and shattered his wrists. He then attempted to integrate Danny, but Danny was saved by an avalanche. After this, he set out to kill the last incarnation of Shou Lao, which was with a girl named Pei, and use its energy to power the Randall Gate, still trying to open a portal to the Diyu to save Heather's soul. While he battled and nearly killed Iron Fist, his ally, Davos killed Gork, the reborn Shou-Lao. However, the plan failed and the Xian god of fire, Zhu Rong arrived, claiming The One had upset the cosmic balance and that the whole city would be destroyed in retribution. He then attacked The One and proceeded to begin destroying the city. Iron Fist then bonded to The One, as both of them were dying. Since The One had wired itself into Rand Tower, the whole tower came to life. Unfortunately, even this was not enough to defeat Zhu Rong, so The One gave up its chi and soul to power Danny so that he could use all his chi at once and fly through Zhu Rong, killing the god.

shu onoru.name: Shu-Onoru
shu onoru.origin: Sho-Onoru was a powerful member of the Black Ring who purchased a young Zula from a Stygian slave merchant. When the Zamballah tribesman was on the verge of manhood, Sho-Onoru sent him to be sold in Khemi. When Zula eventually returned to Kheshatta, he managed to be declared Sho-Onoru's legal heir, inheriting his house and his noble title.

shu tan.name: Shu-Tan
shu tan.origin: Little is known about Shu-Tan. He was born a "poor farmer's son". Shu-Tan was also unschooled and illiterate. After have been exposed to the Source alongside with Xorn and Zorn, Shu-Tan became Oracle and joined Xorn's Celestials. Shu-Tan became the voice of the People of the twin Heavenly Cities of Tu'an.After The Ultimates arrived at Tu'an asking for help in a conflict against the Children of Tomorrow, Xorn ordered Oracle to create a tentative dialogue with The Maker of the Children of Tomorrow. As a result, Oracle was telepathically killed by the Children of Tomorrow's City. Oracle's death sparked a war between the Children and the People.

shub niggurath.name: Shub-Niggurath
shub niggurath.origin: ===Origins=== Shub-Niggurath was either a Great or a Lesser Old One. She was known under a variety of names, such as the Goat with a Thousand Young, the God of a Thousand Young, the Goat God, the Great Goat God or gods, the Black Goat gods, the elder god Sahb Delanzar or simply Delanzar, the Black Beast of Hell with its Thousand Young, and possibly the Devil. The "Thousand Young" represent the babies sacrificed in her name, and are collectively known as the "One Thousand". It is said that these young, as warriors, would "someday lead Sahb Delanzar's avenging army when he comes to consume the Earth" and that he shall inherit all the kingdoms of the world, ruling all of Earth once again. It allegedly ruled all of Earth at some point. ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== thumb|left|380px|The sorcerer sacrificing the goat Devil Butt (Earth-616)|Devil Butt to the "Black Beast of Hell" Circa 28,500 BC or before , in the hills of Zalgara, Valusia, in the middle of summer, an unnamed sorcerer sacrificed seven goats (with Tyre's goat, Devil Butt, being the seventh and last one) in the name of the Black Beast of Hell with its Thousand Young to Yagotha the Guardian of the Gate, to make him turn the Key holding back the Old Ones behind the Gate, intending to have them do his bidding. Though the sorcerer was killed, the summoning was a success and an icy horror came to Earth's dimension to prepare the planet for the Old Ones, until it was defeated and forced into retreat by a hero whose name was forgotten. At some point in the Pre-Cataclysmic Age (see notes on Captain Rhan's page), Captain Ehestes Rhan possessed a few books of ancient incantations (though he claimed never to have dabbled in black magic). Rhan was marooned on an island west of Grebuhl by his crew. Stranded on the island (which he named Zahrahn), Rhan decided to punish the mutineers and to force them to respect the Ancients they despised. He studied the teachings of Set and Mhur in his books. He prayed to the Dark Ones, and to the Great Goat Gods and their brethren, unwillingly summoning a terrible creature only named as "the Were-God". The creature seemingly forced Rhan to mate, and later spawned the monstrous Children of Rhan, rapidly aging girls that eventually transformed into massive feral creatures if they were taken away from their birthplace, and causing the weariness of men. ===Hyborian Age === During the Hyborian Age, Shub-Niggurath was often invoked under various names, and even materialized herself on several occasions. In the city of Zemizar in Zamora, the Goat God was worshipped as Sahb Delanzar (or simply Delanzar). Their worship included the belief that the faithful were taken up to Alabuzar, the Seventh Level of Heaven. The goat was the most sacred of all creatures to Sahb Delanzar's worshippers. Sahb Delanzar's cult was administered by the Brotherhood of Sahb Delanzar, who tried to complete the One Thousand. When Slogg-Nhumazdar came to the city, he pretended fealty to Sahb Delanzar and partnered with the Brotherhood in order to take over the slaughterhouses. The city prospered thanks to the meat trade controlled by the Brotherhood and administered by Slogg, while the Brotherhood gained gold from Slogg's operation. As the Zamoran kings conspired against Zemizar and imposed on its citizens military and economic sanctions, Slogg began selling goat meat at the slaughterhouses to maintain his lifestyle, much to the displeasure of the Brotherhood. Conflict erupted with great damage and casualties, until Slogg offered a truce, stating that he would not sell goat meat any more and would both marry the high priest's daughter, Lissandra, and be supervised in his own house at all times by the high priest himself. Lissandra, in fact, conspired to use the son she had with Slogg as a sacrifice to Sahb Delanzar. Still, in order to afford his lifestyle, Slogg reneged on the truce and started selling goat meat once again, causing tensions with the Brotherhood for the second time. He consequently hired the help of Conan of Cimmeria to protect him from them. thumb|left|240px|The Goat God appearing before the Brotherhood of Sahb Delanzar (Earth-616)|Brotherhood of Sahb Delanzar thumb|right|240px|Sahb Delanzar devouring Slogg-Nhumazdar (Earth-616)|Slogg and Lissandra The Brotherhood (who tried to slay Slogg and take his son as their final sacrifice) soon opposed Conan, whom they viewed as a threat to the ritual. Eventually, the high priest was slain by Slogg and his son was taken by his wife, Lissandra, to the underground altar of the Goat God. Slogg and Conan pursued them there, and decimated the Brotherhood. Lissandra shed her own blood to invoke Sahb Delanzar, drawing the symbol of power on a stone talisman. His appearance caused panic among the worshippers, who all fled for their lives. Sahb Delanzar grasped Conan to devour him, but Conan managed to shatter the stone talisman into pieces, causing pain and loss of strength to the Goat God, and letting Conan tumble

fields.history: ===Origins=== Shub-Niggurath was either a Great or a Lesser Old One. She was known under a variety of names, such as the Goat with a Thousand Young, the God of a Thousand Young, the Goat God, the Great Goat God or gods, the Black Goat gods, the elder god Sahb Delanzar or simply Delanzar, the Black Beast of Hell with its Thousand Young, and possibly the Devil. The "Thousand Young" represent the babies sacrificed in her name, and are collectively known as the "One Thousand". It is said that these young, as warriors, would "someday lead Sahb Delanzar's avenging army when he comes to consume the Earth" and that he shall inherit all the kingdoms of the world, ruling all of Earth once again. It allegedly ruled all of Earth at some point. ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== thumb|left|380px|The sorcerer sacrificing the goat Devil Butt (Earth-616)|Devil Butt to the "Black Beast of Hell" Circa 28,500 BC or before , in the hills of Zalgara, Valusia, in the middle of summer, an unnamed sorcerer sacrificed seven goats (with Tyre's goat, Devil Butt, being the seventh and last one) in the name of the Black Beast of Hell with its Thousand Young to Yagotha the Guardian of the Gate, to make him turn the Key holding back the Old Ones behind the Gate, intending to have them do his bidding. Though the sorcerer was killed, the summoning was a success and an icy horror came to Earth's dimension to prepare the planet for the Old Ones, until it was defeated and forced into retreat by a hero whose name was forgotten. At some point in the Pre-Cataclysmic Age (see notes on Captain Rhan's page), Captain Ehestes Rhan possessed a few books of ancient incantations (though he claimed never to have dabbled in black magic). Rhan was marooned on an island west of Grebuhl by his crew. Stranded on the island (which he named Zahrahn), Rhan decided to punish the mutineers and to force them to respect the Ancients they despised. He studied the teachings of Set and Mhur in his books. He prayed to the Dark Ones, and to the Great Goat Gods and their brethren, unwillingly summoning a terrible creature only named as "the Were-God". The creature seemingly forced Rhan to mate, and later spawned the monstrous Children of Rhan, rapidly aging girls that eventually transformed into massive feral creatures if they were taken away from their birthplace, and causing the weariness of men. ===Hyborian Age === During the Hyborian Age, Shub-Niggurath was often invoked under various names, and even materialized herself on several occasions. In the city of Zemizar in Zamora, the Goat God was worshipped as Sahb Delanzar (or simply Delanzar). Their worship included the belief that the faithful were taken up to Alabuzar, the Seventh Level of Heaven. The goat was the most sacred of all creatures to Sahb Delanzar's worshippers. Sahb Delanzar's cult was administered by the Brotherhood of Sahb Delanzar, who tried to complete the One Thousand. When Slogg-Nhumazdar came to the city, he pretended fealty to Sahb Delanzar and partnered with the Brotherhood in order to take over the slaughterhouses. The city prospered thanks to the meat trade controlled by the Brotherhood and administered by Slogg, while the Brotherhood gained gold from Slogg's operation. As the Zamoran kings conspired against Zemizar and imposed on its citizens military and economic sanctions, Slogg began selling goat meat at the slaughterhouses to maintain his lifestyle, much to the displeasure of the Brotherhood. Conflict erupted with great damage and casualties, until Slogg offered a truce, stating that he would not sell goat meat any more and would both marry the high priest's daughter, Lissandra, and be supervised in his own house at all times by the high priest himself. Lissandra, in fact, conspired to use the son she had with Slogg as a sacrifice to Sahb Delanzar. Still, in order to afford his lifestyle, Slogg reneged on the truce and started selling goat meat once again, causing tensions with the Brotherhood for the second time. He consequently hired the help of Conan of Cimmeria to protect him from them. thumb|left|240px|The Goat God appearing before the Brotherhood of Sahb Delanzar (Earth-616)|Brotherhood of Sahb Delanzar thumb|right|240px|Sahb Delanzar devouring Slogg-Nhumazdar (Earth-616)|Slogg and Lissandra The Brotherhood (who tried to slay Slogg and take his son as their final sacrifice) soon opposed Conan, whom they viewed as a threat to the ritual. Eventually, the high priest was slain by Slogg and his son was taken by his wife, Lissandra, to the underground altar of the Goat God. Slogg and Conan pursued them there, and decimated the Brotherhood. Lissandra shed her own blood to invoke Sahb Delanzar, drawing the symbol of power on a stone talisman. His appearance caused panic among the worshippers, who all fled for their lives. Sahb Delanzar grasped Conan to devour him, but Conan managed to shatter the stone talisman into pieces, causing pain and loss of strength to the Goat God, and letting Conan tumble
weaknesses: The Goat God was seen to feel pain and lose strength after a stone talisman with the eldritch symbol of power used to invoke him was shattered into pieces.
fields.notes: ===Creation and First Appearance=== Robert E. Howard's Shuma-Gorath's name was possibly inspired by Shub-Niggurath's. The Demons' profile in state that Shub-Niggurath first appeared in , where a demon described as "a shapeless mass of cloudy something" was invoked and appeared, unnamed. The profile also lists the Demon of Smoke (a name fitting the description of the monster) as appearing in that issue. The profile also mentions that Zeriti summoned a "smoke demon" of "unknown origin". A website reprising the listing corrected Shub-Niggurath's first appearance or mention to , where the "Great Goat Gods" were invoked. The first named appearance occurred in , where the Great Goat God, the God of a thousand young, is named "Sahb Delanzar". It is unclear if that being is indeed the same, despite the resemblance in the titles. ===Pastiches=== Niggurab, mentioned in (September, 1992), written by Len Kaminski, was considered by the Appendix to the Handbook of the Marvel Universe to be a Marvel reference to Shub-Niggurath. The Demons' profile in listed both Old Ones separately. Shigguraub, mentioned in (July, 1993), written by Rafael Nieves and Len Kaminski, could be an alternate name for either Niggurab or Shub-Niggurath, or another distinct entity altogether. ===Gender=== In H. P. Lovecraft's work, Shub-Niggurath is female. In Marvel Comics, as Shub-Niggurath, the Goat is female, but as "Sahb Delanzar", it is male. ===Names=== Shub-Niggurath is alternatively described as an individual entity (the "Goat with a Thousand Young", the "Goat God"), or as a group (the "Black Goat gods", the "Great Goat gods"). Some of her aliases mention 1,000 young (the "Goat with a Thousand Young", the "God of a thousand young"). In the case of Sahb Delanzar, the "Thousand Young" represent the babies that were sacrificed to him, and were collectively known as the "One Thousand". In , the Great Goat God was named "Sahb Delanzar" or simply "Delanzar". Despite not being called "Shub-Niggurath" and being depicted as a male entity, that entity was seemingly her, as Sahb Delanzar's aliases (the "Goat God", the "Great Goat God", the "God of a Thousand Young") fit with Shub-Niggurath's aliases.
fields.trivia: The Goat God often wondered why suckling babies were sacrificed to him by his followers when there was far more meat on fully grown adults.

shuffler.name: Shuffler
shuffler.origin: The Shuffler was a gambler who lived in the town of Red Dog, Texas during the days of the Golden Egg Gambling Palace. His operation was run out of the Frontier Saloon along with his partners Ace and Dawson. Eventually, the Shuffler and Dawson sought to cut Ace out of their enterprise and plotted to kill him. The opportunity came to them one night when Ace humiliated local drunk Jem Hartley and threw him out of the Frontier Saloon, this altercation ending with Jem threatening to kill Ace. The Shuffler then had Dawson sneak up behind Ace one night and shoot him dead. When Ace's body was discovered, the murder was investigated by sheriff Blaze Carson. Both the Shuffler and Dawson blamed Jem of murdering their partner, recalling the threat from the night before. However, Dawson let slip that Ace was shot with a .44. As Blaze investigated the evidence was looking to stack up against Jem Hartley who surrendered to the law. Meanwhile, the Shuffler and Dawson were working up the locals into a lynch mob in the hopes of getting Jem killed by a mob so they can avoid implication in the murder. However, Blaze kept Jem safe until they got into the sheriff's office. There they were informed by the doctor that the autopsy on Ace was completed and that the bullets that killed him fire clean through his body and were smashed flat, eliminating any sort of way to identify the calibre of the bullets. Remembering that Dawson had told him that they were .44 rounds, Blaze correctly deduced who the real killers were. By this point, the, Shuffler was leading a lynch mob to the sheriff's office. The mob stood down when Blaze and the Doc appeared with guns. Jem then accused Dawson of killing Ace and framing him. When Dawson denied the allegations, Jem became enraged and began beating on Dawson who surrendered and confessed to the crime. Dawson and the Shuffler were then arrested and locked in jail. The Shuffler's subsequent fate is unknown.

shuma gorath.name: Shuma-Gorath
shuma gorath.origin: ===Origins=== Shuma-Gorath was one of the Great Old Ones also named Many-Angled Ones, extradimensional beings predating Earth and possibly the universe itself. He was spawned in a dimension diametrically opposed to Earth's dimension. At some point, Shuma-Gorath created Quoggoth, as a servant. right|thumb|300px|Quoggoth (Earth-616)|Quoggoth's rebellion against Shuma-Gorath Eons before the current time, Shuma-Gorath fought the Elders of the Universe who were joined by the abstract entity the In-Betweener. ===Early Reign on Earth=== Ruler of hundreds of dimensions, Shuma-Gorath came to the Earth-Realm million years ago along with the other Old Ones, ruling the Earth and feasting on the ape-men. Hundred of millions of years ago, Quoggoth rebelled, fancying himself more powerful than his creator. Shuma-Gorath defeated Quoggoth but couldn't destroy him, so imprisoned him in the island that became for a time Magneto's base in the Modern Age. ===1,000,000 BC=== Some time around 1,000,000 years ago, he was banished from the Earth-Realm by the time-traveling sorcerer Sise-Neg. This was all observed by another time-traveling sorcerer, Doctor Strange, who had hoped to defeat Shuma-Gorath in the past so that his master, the Ancient One, would not need to die in a future conflict with the demon. Also circa 1,000,000 BC, Shuma-Gorath attempted to invade the Earth but was defeated by the prehistoric Avengers. ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age === Shuma-Gorath somehow managed to return, allegedly drifting to Earth millenias before the Great Cataclysm, and again set himself up as a god. The god-thing fed himself on blood sacrifice rituals and tribal war, but any priest or shaman who sought his favor by organizing sacrifices and wars was also killed. After an age of Shuma-Gorath's torturous rule, some sent out a cry to a new god, Crom. Crom sent a storm of the Northlands, and with it three iron-bound books and a key to unlock them. Armed with the books, a shaman went to confront Shuma-Gorath. He read aloud from the books atop a mountain, and just before he finished the third volume, a vengeful Shuma-Gorath incinerated the mortal with a blast of energy. A flame-headed cloud rose from the ashes, however, sealing Crom's spell, and imprisoning Shuma-Gorath within the mountain. The mountain was later named Mount Crom in the avenging god's honor. The three books became known as the Iron-Bound Books of Shuma-Gorath. The Vishanti and Shuma-Gorath were eventually known to each other some time after the formation of the mystic trinity and became bitter foes to this day, neither succeeding in destroying the other. ===Hyborian Age === During the the Hyborian Age, the sorcerer Kulan Gath and the witch-queen of Hyperborea Vammatar fought with their two armies to a standstill. Negotiating, Vammatar revealed that she had the Iron-Bound Books of Shuma-Gorath, while Kulan Gath had the key to open them. Vammatar proposed an alliance sealed by marriage, which would allow them to work together to release Shuma-Gorath and command his power for their own. At the base of Mount Crom, Vammatar turned on Gath, and while they fought Crom sent down a bolt of lightning that created an avalanche. The books were buried, and the newlywed sorcerers were separated, each believing the other to be dead for many years to come. A century later, Vammatar came into conflict with the young warrior Conan of Cimmeria. At one point, the sorceress set fire to the Village of the Snow Bear where Conan was raised in order to clear a path to Mount Crom. Conan received a dream of its destruction (possibly a vision from his deity, Crom) in which the name "Shuma-Gorath" was chanted repeatedly. With his traveling companion Hobb, Conan headed north to confront the sorceress and her Witch-Men. Once he arrived at Mount Crom, however, Shuma-Gorath took control of Hobb's mind and compelled him to read from the Iron-Bound Books, freeing him from his mountain prison. By this time Vammatar had been joined by Kulan Gath, and for a time the pair seemed to hold the demon with their spells. He was not under their control, however, and the pair were obliterated as Shuma-Gorath finished relating the tale of his imprisonment. Conan took up the books, and used their power to resist the demon's attacks. Shuma-Gorath offered Conan immense power if he would stop, but Conan refused. Instead, Conan threw the books from the mountaintop to the storm above, returning them to Crom. Crom's power then once again sealed Shuma-Gorath in one of his home dimensions. thumb|300px|left ===19th Century=== In 1804, a cult that worshipped Shuma-Gorath was formed in the United States in the land where the Ravencroft Institute would be built many years later. ===Modern Age=== ====Battling Strange==== In modern times, Doctor Strange and his mentor, the Ancient One came under a series of attacks by beings such as Nightmare, Sligguth, Ebora, N'Gabthoth, Dagoth, Kathulos, and the Living Buddha. At one point, Strange detected a pecu

fields.notes: Shuma Gorath and his iron-bound books were first mentioned in Robert E. Howard's Kull short story "The Curse of the Golden Skull." It was believed to be either the name of a deity or a cult. The name was possibly inspired by H.P. Lovecraft's Shub-Niggurath, and is to be related to the Cthulhu Mythos. The name was first mentioned in Marvel Comics in the adaptation of "Dig Me No Grave" (February, 1937) in , written by Roy Thomas. The adaptation mentions Shuma-Gorath, instead of Yog-Sothoth and Kathulos in the original story, and Acheron, in place of Yuggoth. Robert E. Howard's creation, limited to a name, was then adapted into a being, mentioned in , written by Gardner Fox, and fully appeared in issue . The Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe sometime erroneously list Shuma-Gorath as first appearing in (November, 1972), which is actually its first mention in the adventures of Doctor Strange, ignoring its mention in "Dig Me No Grave" ( ; October, 1972). Due to legal complications involving the name "Shuma-Gorath," the character has been referred to as Gargantos in recent appearances. The first instance of this was Gargantos from . However, scriptwriter Michael Waldron stated in the director's commentary for the film that the MCU's Gargantos was "not to be confused with" Shuma-Gorath, complicating matters. The Marvel Legends figure based on Shuma-Gorath from the Marvel vs. Capcom series was given the name "Gargantos" instead. The character is referred to as "Gargantos" in . The writer, Steve Orlando, has confirmed this is due to legal issues.
fields.trivia: Shuma-Gorath is one of Marvel's Cthulhu pastiches. Death has referred to Shuma-Gorath with gender neutral pronouns. Shagreen, a sorcerer from an alien dimension, invoked an entity known as "Cthuma-Gurath," which may have been another name used by Shuma-Gorath. Additionally, a character known as Nyarla-Gorath was summoned by Squid Kid, though any relation with Shuma-Gorath is unspecified. Shuma-Gorath was chosen as part of the roster of Marvel Super Heroes by Capcom due to the character's unique appearance. Since he had few appearances at the time of the game's development, Marvel's licensing department purportedly did not initially know who Shuma-Gorath was, and allowed Capcom almost complete creative freedom in regards to the character due to Marvel viewing him as having no commercial value. By the time that entered development, Shuma-Gorath was the first character that Capcom asked Marvel to include in their side of the roster. Marvel was reluctant at first, but Capcom convinced them that Shuma-Gortah was popular to the fighting game franchise, and an important part of its history.

shuri.origin: ===The Child of the Panther=== The Princess of Wakanda, Shuri was the only child of Queen Ramonda with King T'Chaka. Her father was tragically assassinated by the colonialist Ulysses Klaw before her birth. From a very young age, the orphaned Shuri wanted to claim her position as an heiress to the throne of Wakanda by becoming the legendary hero of her people known as the Black Panther. Following King T'Chaka's demise, his brother S'Yan ascended as the interim monarch and Black Panther, constantly duelling warriors who could battle for the role he had never wished for. Queen Ramonda was contrary to the young Shuri's wishes of participating in the challenge and attempted to restrain her with no success. As Shuri broke into the arena to confront her uncle S'Yan for the mantle of the Black Panther, she witnessed another fighter defeat him and acquire the title, her older paternal half-brother, T'Challa. thumb|left|250px|Shuri's first kill Under the shadow of T'Challa, the Black Panther, the young Shuri was constantly cast out from affairs concerning Wakanda, for her family wished to keep her away from danger. Alternatively, she pursued an education in nuclear physics. When the Vibranium deposits in Wakanda seemed to be the cause of incoming disasters, Shuri remarked that the Vibranium itself could have been tampered with, but got ignored by the Black Panther. She was proven correct when Klaw invaded Wakanda alongside a legion of super-villains with secret support from leaderships from all over the globe. The research facility where Shuri was in got raided by the Radioactive Man, who murdered the miner Q'Ran in cold blood in front of Shuri, forcing her to hide. The villain prepared to obliterate the location with a nuclear explosion to serve Klaw's purposes. Furtively, Shuri stroke back. Finding Black Knight's Ebony Blade in the fight, she wielded it to slain her opponent. The invasion was stopped and Klaw got destroyed. The experience of killing someone proved to be difficult to Shuri, who coped by retreating to the United States for a period of time. In order to provide assistance to his sister, T'Challa trained her in hand-to-hand combat. Part of his intentions included the expectation that she could take his place as Black Panther should a day come when she needed to lead Wakanda. Despite being particularly headstrong and excessively angry, the will to become the Black Panther drove Shuri to become a gifted fighter as time went by. ===War with Atlantis=== Shuri, as queen of Wakanda, was involved in treaty negotiations with Namor, who offered to end the bloodshed between their two nations in exchange for refuge in Wakanda whenever he desired. This same treaty was first presented to T'Challa, who originally rejected it. Like her brother, Shuri also declined Namor's offer stating that the conflict between the two nations was no ordinary war, and that the fate of both Wakanda or Atlantis hung in the balance; in the end, one of them would face total destruction. While Namor was celebrating the fabricated peace with T'Challa, T'Challa revealed the truth, and Namor left to find Atlantis a ruin by Shuri's forces after an attack by Wakanda. ===Time Runs Out=== With the incursions threatening the existence of the universe and the Earth, Namor formed a Cabal to do what the Illuminati were unable to bring themselves to do, destroy incoming colliding alternate Earths. The Cabal took over Wakanda and turned it into their base of operations, razing the Golden City and slaughtering its citizens. In an attempt to disrupt the Cabal's stolen arsenal of Antimatter Injection Systems, Shuri and T'Challa found themselves cornered by Proxima Midnight of the Cabal. Shuri remained behind to confront their enemies while T'Challa teleported away, at his sister's request. thumb|left|As the Black Panther ===Djalia=== Shuri was defeated by the Cabal's forces and trapped within a construct of amber similar to Thane's, a construct which left her in a state of stasis known as "living death." As Black Panther struggled to find a way to bring his sister's body back to life, Shuri's soul made its way to the Djalia, a transcendent plane that represented Wakanda's collective memory. During her time in the Djalia, Shuri trained with and learned from a Griot that had taken the form of Ramonda. T'Challa eventually resurrected Shuri by retrieving her soul with the help of Manifold. Now imbued with wisdom and new powers, Shuri confronted Aneka, a Dora Milaje and one of the leaders of a rebellious group. Shuri seemingly convinced Aneka and Ayo to stand with the Black Panther in the wake of the invasion of another rebellion led by Tetu, which marched towards the Golden City. ===Imperial=== The new democratic system of Wakanda proved proved to be too unsustainable, and seeing that it just could not work, the nation returned to a constitutional monarchy. T'Challa retook the throne of not just Wakanda, but of its Intergalactic Empire. Shuri joined him on W

shuten doji.name: Shuten Döji
shuten doji.origin: Shuten Döji was a former member of The Hand who broke out on his own. He established a base of operations in Bagalia, built himself an army of ninja, and started amassing high-tech arsenal. Shuten's enemies put a contract out on him, and the assingment was taken by Deadpool. Deadpool initially joined a group of mercenaries that had taken the job and approached Shuten Döji's castle on a plane. Their presence was detected by Shuten, and he ordered his men to take it down. After killing the mercenaries since there was also a hit on their head, Deadpool launched their corpses on jetpacks on Shuten Döji's castle as a distraction. By the time Deadpool landed and started slaughtering Shuten's army of monks and ninja, the warlord had already retreated. After killing Shuten's army, Deadpool delved deeper into the castle and was confronted by Shuten himself, who appeared to have had grafted into his body mechanical arms similar to Doctor Octopus' Tentacles. Shuten Döji rapidly constricted Deadpool and pulled him up close. However, Deadpool had stolen a glove that mimicked Iron Fist's powers from one of Shuten's ninja, and punched Shuten Döji on the face with it, which blew off his entire head.

shzzzllzzzthzz.name: Shzzzllzzzthzz
shzzzllzzzthzz.origin: The Blip is a member of a peaceful alien race composed completely of electrical energy. The Blip had been on a mission of peace to another galaxy for two months before he left to return home. However, while traveling back to his home dimension, he became trapped in a space-time warp. It took nearly all of his power to free himself from the warp, after which he decided to set down on the nearest habitable planet to recharge. He landed on Earth, and began absorbing all of the electrical energy from the surrounding area. As a result, military radar and the town of Oakville lost their power. Seeking the cause for the sudden power outage, a radar operator stumbled across the Blip, who told him his story. Unknown to either being, the townspeople also were looking for the source of the power outage and were armed with rifles. When the Blip tried to greet them, they mistook him for a monster and opened fire. They then attacked the radar operator, believing him to be a traitor. This enraged the Blip, who had never before seen a race capable of such savagery. He quickly dispatched the mob, and told them that they were not worthy of the secrets which he could have shared with them. He then departed for the stars, hoping that the next time that their races met, humanity will by then have grown up. At some unrevealed point, a second member of the Blip's race came to Earth and died in unrevealed circumstances. Frank Johnson came into possession of the creature's remains, as well as those of Rorgg, the Two-Headed Thing, and Grottu, all of which he displayed in his "Museum of the Monstrous and Strange". The creatures were all later revived and battled the Fantastic Four, though they were quickly defeated. A Blip later appeared on Monster Isle when Shadowcat and Magik went looking for a mutant girl named Bo. The Blip was among the monsters that attacked the three until Magik teleported herself, Shadowcat, and Bo to the Jean Grey School for Higher Learning. During the Leviathons' invasion, the Blip was among the monsters that appeared in San Diego. Blip assisted in fighting the Leviathons. ===Phony Blips=== The image of the creature known as the Blip has been utilized many times since his first appearance. The earliest known time, Shzzzllzzzthzz's image was used was about 10 years before the Heroic Age by the dream demon known as Nightmare. Nightmare had created a duplicate of the Blip, along with several other monsters, to haunt a young Peter Parker in his dreams. Years later, early on in the career of the Fantastic Four, Mister Fantastic created another duplicate of the Blip, along with others of Fin Fang Foom, It! the Living Colossus, and Sporr to attack Doctor Doom after he had stolen the power of Galactus. The giant monsters were a successful distraction, allowing Mister Fantastic to recover the Cosmic Cube and restore everything to normal. Sometime later, Xemnu the Living Titan created a duplicate of the Blip, as well as duplicates of Diablo, Groot, Goom, and Taboo, using them to attack the Hulk. The Hulk, however, destroyed all of the duplicates.

The creatures were all later revived and battled the Fantastic Four, though they were quickly defeated. A Blip later appeared on Monster Isle when Shadowcat and Magik went looking for a mutant girl named Bo. The Blip was among the monsters that attacked the three until Magik teleported herself, Shadowcat, and Bo to the Jean Grey School for Higher Learning. During the Leviathons' invasion, the Blip was among the monsters that appeared in San Diego. Blip assisted in fighting the Leviathons. ===Phony Blips=== The image of the creature known as the Blip has been utilized many times since his first appearance. The earliest known time, Shzzzllzzzthzz's image was used was about 10 years before the Heroic Age by the dream demon known as Nightmare. Nightmare had created a duplicate of the Blip, along with several other monsters, to haunt a young Peter Parker in his dreams. Years later, early on in the career of the Fantastic Four, Mister Fantastic created another duplicate of the Blip, along with others of Fin Fang Foom, It! the Living Colossus, and Sporr to attack Doctor Doom after he had stolen the power of Galactus. The giant monsters were a successful distraction, allowing Mister Fantastic to recover the Cosmic Cube and restore everything to normal. Sometime later, Xemnu the Living Titan created a duplicate of the Blip, as well as duplicates of Diablo, Groot, Goom, and Taboo, using them to attack the Hulk. The Hulk, however, destroyed all of the duplicates.
weaknesses: The Blip has proven vulnerable to grounding and short-circuiting.

si ma.name: Si Ma
si ma.origin: Si Ma and her colleague Nero were scientists who worked for Bio-Armor, a technological research firm contracted by the Stark Defense Corporation. Under the leadership of SDC's founder Howard Stark, Si Ma and Nero were instrumental in creating a bacterial body sheathe that would render an individual impervious to most conventional forms of injury.Howard Stark lost controlling interest in Stark Defense Corporation to his rival Zebediah Stane, but fortunately, Stane had no legal ownership over projects designed by Bio-Armor. Following the birth of Howard's son Antonio, Si Ma contributed to the process that bonded the infant with the Bio-Armor technology. She continued to work for Howard Stark and served as the primary personal physician for young Antonio.

siapep.name: Siapep
siapep.origin: ===Origins=== Siapep was the spawn of the Elder God Set, and the sibling of the Dragon of the Moon, Sligguth, Damballah, Yamata no Orochi, Tartessus, and Ishiti. Siapep the Devourer was associated with the Egyptian gods. It was a servant to the Death god Seth and obeyed his commands. ===Modern Age=== In the modern age, Seth sought revenge against his brother Osiris and the Asgardian thunder god Thor. After capturing Osiris, Seth then went to Earth and captured Thor, taking the Fantastic Four's Thing along with the thunder god to Celestial Heliopolis to battle on the Golden Path of the Gods. In the ensuing battle Seth summoned the Devourer and set it upon the two heroes. The creature was nearly indestructible but was defeated when the Thing pushed off it the Golden Path into the dimensional void below where it has presumably been lost ever since.

sibarthu.name: Sibarthu
sibarthu.origin: Sibarthu was a gigantic bat-lizard entity positioned as an idol and guardian at the Mountain-Temple of God Zokk. The creature remained dormant for centuries until it was awakened by Klonus the Wizard. Klonus used Sibarthu as both a flying mount and an ally during his assault on Citrusville. After teleporting there with Mortak, Klonus forced Dakimh, Jennifer Kale, Korrek, and Man-Thing into battle. While Klonus fought Dakhim and Mortak confronted Korrek, Sibarthu attacked Man-Thing directly. During the struggle, Man-Thing used a roadside sign to decapitate the creature. Upon touching the ground, Sibarthu’s severed head reverted to its original stone form, causing the entire monster to collapse into lifeless rubble.

sibylla.name: Sibylla
sibylla.origin: From a young age, Sibylla possessed the power to see into the future. So, she became an oracle for the temple of Apollo and Artemis and acted as a deliverer for their messages to mortals. When Sibylla was about to succumb to old age, Apollo offered godhood, but she rejected the offer so she her spirit could remain in the temple and act as a guide for her successors. When the Roman Empire of an alternate reality conquered the galaxy but ran out of enemies, the mad wizard Xennus decided to use the temple of Mt. Gaurus as a pathway into other realities for the Roman Empire to conquer. To stop Xennus, Sibylla asked Doctor Strange and Clea for their help. Clea, Sibylla, and the spirit of the oracle Thaleia worked together to close the portal and send Xennus back to his home reality. With her job done, Sibylla's body crumbled away, and the temple collapsed. Sibylla later reappeared on Earth-616 and somehow became head of the Federal Reserve. When Kang the Conqueror began killing off the Avengers by killing them as babies, Hercules asked for her help. Sibylla gave Hercules her amulet, which he and Avengers could use to protect themselves from Kang's meddling of the timeline.

sickle moon.name: Sickle Moon
sickle moon.origin: A ruthless hitman who was assigned to kill Nate McBride by The Cheese, but the crimelord was punished by Foolkiller. So, he killed Nate without payment before learning of his employers death. A year later, the racist gang the White Angels called him to kill Punisher as they were being hunted by him and Foolkiller, and wanted to kill Foolkiller themselves. On the plane from New York to Los Angeles, he killed a selfish fat woman who was seated near him. He almost killed the Punisher with his crescent shaped blades before his arm was slashed off by Foolkiller. He then fell off the bridge into the river with both vigilantes thinking he was dead. He survived the fall, went home and promised revenge on Foolkiller while attaching his new mechanical arm and trying it by killing a cat.

sico rudo.name: Sico Rudo
sico rudo.origin: Professor Sico Rudo was a Imperial Japanese scientist who was active during World War II. By the summer of 1945, he developed a weapon for the Japanese he called "Atom Water", a liquid that when evaporated caused a powerful explosion. To test it out, he and a group of Japanese soldiers used it on a Japanese island that recently was captured by the Americans, with each sample going off in areas that the military were clearing. The blasts prompted Captain America and Bucky to investigate it further. Following the trail of explosions to the cave where Rudo and his men were hiding out, Cap and Bucky were captured. Rudo then left them tied up in the sun surrounded by Atom Water and left a sample vial behind to mock them while they went to cause more destruction. Breaking free, Cap tossed the sample vial into Rudo's cave. Tracking down Rudo and his men, Cap and Bucky attacked. With his men losing the battle, Rudo shot his own men and fled back to his cave. When Cap and Bucky failed to follow them, he accused them of being cowards just moments before the broken vial of Atom Water exploded, killing him instantly. Recovering a sample of Atom Water from one of the dead soldiers, Cap turned it over to the military where he was informed America had developed a more powerful weapon: The Atom Bomb.

sid brute.origin: Sid Brute was the director of the grade C film "Sump Thing", produced by Ted Silverberg. At yet another hiccup during filming, he timidly told Silverberg that they still had enough swell footage to make it a super-blockbuster, but not convincing Silverberg at all. Later he had to direct the Thing in a film where a monster attacked Tokyo and he had to rush to its defense and save the city and introducing himself to Ben he told him how the scenes should take place, and when the Thing said why a monster had to attack Tokyo, Sid replied that it was a silly question as monsters always attack Tokyo.

sid ridley.origin: "Rambling" Sid Ridley, as Captain Midlands, is the British equivalent of Captain America. The British Super Soldier program of the early 1940s increased his strength, stamina, and agility to the peak of human capacity. This allowed him to fight as a British Super Soldier during World War II. Captain Midlands, unlike Captain America, was not frozen in ice and aged normally. Captain Midlands is now in his 80s but he still has his superhuman abilities but has the aged body of a pensioner. Much of Sid Ridley's life remains a mystery but he did marry Nancy Ridley who died in 1963. This was Captain Midland's greatest loss and when offered his heart's desire by the Duke of Hell known as Plokta, his wish was to live happily with her. After the Skrull invasion of Earth, Captain Midlands spent his time protecting the citizens of the United Kingdom from drug smugglers and other such more mundane criminals. During one of the drug busts on the Cloverleaf Estate in Hodge Hill, Birmingham he found Plokta, the Duke of Hell's secret base, which he has set up for his plans taking over the planet. Captain Midlands battled the Mindless Ones but due to the number he was forced to surrender. He sent out a distress call to MI13 team bringing them to Plokta's base to save him. When they found Captain Midlands he tricked them into entering the dream corridor which trapped them and used their magical energies to create more Mindless Ones to attack Earth. Captain Midlands was working for the Duke of Hell since he was captured and offered his heart's desire; his long dead wife Nancy. Pete Wisdom destroyed Captain Midlands' fantasy and MI13 escaped from the dream corridor to defeat Plokta. Captain Midlands was taken away and declared a traitor to the crown and put in the Vault, a high security prison in Shoreditch, to await trial. Before the trial, Pete Wisdom visited Captain Midlands in his cell and gave him a gun so that he could shoot himself rather than go through a trial for treason. Though whether or not he took this oppurtunity is left ambiguous.

sidney abel.name: Sidney Abel
sidney abel.origin: thumb|left|150px|Sidney after the transformationSidney Abel was a simple person but physically small to the point of not even being accepted into the Army, so he started working in a laboratory that carried out research for the Army and he in particular took care of the guinea pigs they used for their experiments. When he had to place guinea pigs on an island where they would detonate a nuclear warhead, he decided to stay on the island since his life had little meaning. However, he did not die with the bomb explosion but received a high dose of radiation that modified his DNA and physically transformed him, making him a tall and muscular man, the one he had always dreamed of. Escaping from the research center, Sidney returned to his city to first meet his best friend Bill, who was afraid of him as he was contaminated, and then he went to Nancy's house, the girl with whom Sidney was in love but to whom he had never declared himself due to his physical appearance. Nancy chased him away, telling him that she didn't recognize him as Sidney, who she remembered as a sweet and kind person while he was a monster. She also told him that her parents had both died from shock upon hearing the news of what had happened to him. Rejected by everyone, at that point Sidney decided to retreat to the contaminated island in the company of the only beings who would accept him, his guinea pigs.

sidney crumb.name: Sidney Crumb
sidney crumb.origin: thumb|left|175px Sid Crumb was a poor boy in his early life which he was beaten on by bullies and had to deal with a drunk father at home. In his later years, he was married and spent most of his time drinking, at one point his wife Mavis had left him. Then one day he heard a strange noise which lead him to the Fury defeated by Captain Britain which it had sent a dart attack accurately killing one of his neighbors to regenerate. As he ran, it sent a dart attack at him only hitting him in the arm in which the narrator says "such good fortune could never be Sid's", the dart was laced with a poison that slowly mutated him. He was slightly aware of the transformation thinking he was sick but wasn't completely. Later, he was in the rain as the mutation slowly took over. He then went over to some kids cutting school in hopes of finding help, but he had a flashback about the bullies and blindly dissolved them. As he continued, the mutation caused him to grow while his body seemed to already be dead. As he moved onward, the mutation caused his fingers to change: one became a tentacle, two stayed the same, one was a big mound of rotting flesh, and one was a normal human arm. While he changed, he lost his clothes and his mouth. thumb|200px|left Soon, he had a flashback about his drunken father and Mavis thinking "You've could've stayed!" while he decided to "show her". He went to a pharmacy to get tablets, but then realized his mouth was gone and he thought loudly "WHERE"S MY MOUTH?!" While he did this, he picked up two people dissolving them to look for his mouth, and Captain Britain came and fought him. While Sid recognized him, he flashed back to the Fury that had caused the accident and hit Captain Britain thinking nobody cared for him. As Captain Britain hit him back, it started to hurt him until he screamed in his mind "PLEASE STOP HURTING ME!!" and Captain Britain felt it as he slowly dissolved away.

sidney green.name: Sidney Green
sidney green.origin: ===Origin=== Sidney Green grew up in a number of orphanages and foster homes in New Jersey. He was a boorish, clumsy child and suffered from chronic bedwetting, carrying around with him the funk of uncleanliness. Because of it Sidney was ostracized by other kids and was often the target of cruel bullying not only by them, but even the adults. To suppress bedwetting Sidney avoided liquids, but it led to dizziness and dehydration. All of it turned his life miserable and resulted in depression and self-worth issues. After his mutation activated, his body was severely changed, including his lower half. Finally he was no longer suffering from bedwetting. ===Xavier Institute=== Sidney was accepted into the Xavier Institute and joined Gambit's Squad as Onyxx. As a mutant, Sidney had regained some confidence, forwarding audacious advances to aesthetically stirring female student Foxx. When Foxx was exposed as Mystique, Onyxx was devastated. He confronted "Foxx", demanding what she should admit that she is in love with him, but she beat him severely and smashed his head with a toilet. Within days, Sidney was able to walk again, yet, the experience triggered unfortunate memories of his childhood, perhaps permanently traumatizing him. ===After M-Day=== Sidney retained his powers after the M-Day and remained a resident at the Institute. He participated in the battle for the membership in the New X-Men, but wasn't chosen by Emma Frost. When Purifiers attacked the Institute, Onyxx was critically injured by Reverend William Stryker and barely survived. He and Bling were considering to leave the Institute after all of these events, but eventually stayed. Onyxx was later captured alongside his fellow students by Belasco and imprisoned in Limbo. ===San Francisco and Utopia=== thumb|right|200px|Death Onyxx joined the X-Men when they relocated to San Francisco and later to Utopia and was seen training with Colossus and Rockslide. During the attack of Selene's Inner Circle on Utopia, Onyxx was killed by Wither. ===Krakoa=== Years later Krakoa nation was established and many mutants were resurrected by the Five, including Onyxx. He participated in the second Hellfire Gala.

sidney joern.name: Sidney Joern
sidney joern.origin: Dr. Sidney Joern was a brilliant but unethical scientist and the chief psychic surgeon of a clandestine organization known as the Project, which specialized in illegal psychic surgery performed on unwilling subjects. Under Joern’s direction, the Project sought to control, suppress, or weaponize individuals with extraordinary mental abilities. Joern played a central role in the manipulation and abuse of Mary Walker, later known as Typhoid Mary, whose mutant powers attracted the Project’s attention. Mary was abducted and subjected to repeated psychic experimentation, exacerbating her dissociative identity disorder. When Mary later attempted to force Joern to use psychic surgery to eliminate her violent personalities, Joern instead attempted to kill her during the procedure. The operation was interrupted by Wolverine, leading to a violent confrontation in which Joern shot one of his own assistants and attempted to murder both Mary and Wolverine. Wolverine ultimately decapitated Joern. Despite this, the Project preserved Joern’s severed head, sustaining his consciousness in a nutrient bath. Following these events, the Project was reorganized and renamed Fortress.

sidney levine lmd.name: Sidney Levine (LMD)
sidney levine lmd.origin: This Life Model Decoy of S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Sidney Levine was created by the Encoders under the orders of the Deltite, an advanced LMD created by Arnim Zola who replaced several S.H.I.E.L.D. operatives with LMDs, including the Executive Council. The real Sidney Levine was replaced behind the scenes, and his LMD became active when Nick Fury directed a mission to obtain the S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier's Power Core in the deserts of New Mexico; Levine contacted Hydra, which arrived to battle S.H.I.E.L.D. in order to take the Core for theirselves. The Gaffer's LMD partecipated at Clay Quartermain's funeral. Levine was later revealed to be part of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Roxxon's Project: Delta, the program that replaced agents with LMDs. When the S.H.I.E.L.D. Space Station exploded, all the LMDs were destroyed, including Gaffer's LMD.

The real Sidney Levine was replaced behind the scenes, and his LMD became active when Nick Fury directed a mission to obtain the S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier's Power Core in the deserts of New Mexico; Levine contacted Hydra, which arrived to battle S.H.I.E.L.D. in order to take the Core for theirselves. The Gaffer's LMD partecipated at Clay Quartermain's funeral. Levine was later revealed to be part of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Roxxon's Project: Delta, the program that replaced agents with LMDs. When the S.H.I.E.L.D. Space Station exploded, all the LMDs were destroyed, including Gaffer's LMD.

sidney onselm.name: Sidney Onselm
sidney onselm.origin: The origins of the Brain are unknown, his namesake comes from the fact that he has a massive head. By 1947 he was a leader of his own gang and a regular accomplice of another criminal known only as the Knife. In the summer of that year he and his gang plotted to steal a shipment of Ambergris that was being brought into the United States aboard a ship piloted by Captain Cole. Their intent was to sell the stolen merchandise to perfume manufacturers and make a massive profit. After plotting their caper, the Brain and his men went to their secondary hideout located on Taboo Island to meet up with the knife. They arrived just as the Sub-Mariner and Namora had finished subduing the Knife after stumbling upon him on the island. The Brain took Namora hostage at gun point and forced Namor to stand down. They then tied up the two heroes and were about to kill them when one of the Brain's men informed them that Cole's ship was approaching. The Brian and the Knife were forced to deal with the heroes later while they left to steal the Ambergris. However, Namor and Namora managed to break free of their bonds and track the Brain and his men to Captain Cole's ship where they quickly subdued them and turned them over to the authorities. The subsequent fate of the Brain is unknown.
